writeup: TIC 19569810 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 7.0062 days. Automated analysis of TESS photometry detected a primary eclipse causing 10.92% dimming, along with a secondary eclipse at 8.3 sigma significance. The combined detection signal reaches 156.2 on the Box Least Squares scale. Pixel-level imaging analysis yielded a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 27.9, though the centroid offset of 3.5 arcsec warrants caution: the system's centroid lies only 0.052 pixels closer to the target star than to a nearby bright neighbor, falling within TESS's known centroid systematic uncertainty of 0.10-0.3 pixels. This means TESS's resolution cannot confidently distinguish whether the signal originates from the target star or the neighboring star.
